scene: Inferno XXVIII — ninth bolgia, sowers of discord, wounds that close before the sword returns
story: Dante and Virgil look down into the ninth bolgia, a circuit of souls punished for sowing religious, civic and familial division.
A sword-bearing demon opens wounds as souls pass; by the time they return around the circuit their wounds have closed, only to be inflicted again.

Dante encounters Muhammad, depicted in the poem as divided, and Ali, depicted with a split face; this is Dante's hostile medieval religious portrayal, not an objective account of Islam or its figures.
Pier da Medicina speaks of coming treachery and points to Curio, whose tongue has been severed; Mosca dei Lamberti also appears with his hands mutilated.
Bertran de Born holds his severed head like a lantern and describes his punishment for dividing father and son.
The cycle of healing followed by renewed wounding continues; the healed interval is not a release from the bolgia.
Dante and Virgil continue toward the tenth bolgia, which belongs to the next stage.
